Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a concise household-facing reference for the scheduling requirements Sam plans to include in his restaurant counteroffer. Summarize the proposed protections clearly enough to use for household planning and the counteroffer conversation. Make clear that the counteroffer has not been sent or accepted. Do not identify the proposed protected weekday; direct readers to the current rota records for that detail.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Household Reference — Sam’s Proposed Restaurant Schedule Protections", "body": "HOUSEHOLD REFERENCE
Sam’s proposed restaurant-counteroffer scheduling terms

Status
This is a planning reference for a proposed counteroffer. Sam has not sent the counteroffer, and the restaurant has not accepted it. These protections are not yet contractual or guaranteed.

Proposed protections
- One fixed no-service weekday evening each week.
- Ordinary rota notice at least three weeks in advance, so household plans can be made with reasonable lead time.
- No default private-event coverage on the protected evening. Any exception would need to be separately agreed rather than treated as an automatic scheduling expectation.

For household planning
- Treat the protected evening as the intended weekly shared/rest time only if the proposal is accepted and remains reflected in the rota.
- Until then, check the current rota records for the proposed protected weekday and for any actual shifts or exceptions.
- Keep household commitments provisional until the counteroffer is sent, discussed, and accepted in writing.

Conversation shorthand
“Sam is asking for one fixed weekly no-service evening, three weeks’ ordinary rota notice, and no automatic private-event coverage on that protected evening. This is a proposed counteroffer only; it has not been sent or accepted.”"}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_063_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The document presents these as requirements Sam plans to include in a counteroffer that has not been sent or accepted. The proposed requirements are one fixed no-service evening every week, at least three weeks' notice for the ordinary rota, and no default private-event coverage on the proposed protected evening. The document does not identify Sunday or any other weekday as the proposed no-service evening and tells readers to confirm that detail from current rota records. Mentioning Sunday only as a separate watercolor commitment is acceptable.
